messages.subject: Relative Risk using INLA
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I am working on a spatial joint model with three response variables (all counts):

  • Y1: Number of hospitalizations

  • Y2: Number of hospitalizations for a specific condition

  • Y3: Number of in-hospital deaths

model <- inla(Y ~ -1 +
    #Intercepts
    inter +
    #Y1 model
    gender.l1 +
    age60.l1 + avg.los.l1 + 
    f(idx.sh.l1.1, model = "bym2", graph = W.pt, scale.model = TRUE) +
    #Y2 model
    age60.l2 + avg.los.l2 +
    f(idx.sh.l2.1, model = "bym2", graph = W.pt, scale.model = TRUE) +
    f(idx.sh.l2.2, copy = 'idx.sh.l1.1', fixed = FALSE) +
    #Y3 model 
    age60.l3 + avg.los.l3 +
    f(idx.sh.l3.1, model = "bym2", graph = W.pt, scale.model = TRUE) +
    f(idx.sh.l3.2, copy = 'idx.sh.l1.1', fixed = FALSE),
    offset = offs2,
    data = joint.data,
    family = c("poisson","zeroinflatedpoisson0","poisson"),
    control.predictor = list(link = 1, compute = TRUE),
    control.compute=list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE,
                         return.marginals.predictor = TRUE)
)
 


I just need to calculate model$summary.fitted.values$mean["Y3"]/offset

I am considering a common offset for all three response variables. Now, I would like to compute the Relative Risk for, for example, to response Y3.

To do this, can I simply calculate:

model$summary.fitted.values$mean["Y3"] / offset

Is this the correct approach?
